title: NDA template
line: Both sides keep what they share private.
when: Use it before you share plans, prices, code or client names with someone you may work with.
It runs both ways, so each side is bound by the same promise.
check: Name what counts as confidential, in your own words.
Set how long the promise lasts.
Check the state whose law should apply.
summary: Two sides share private information and each agrees to protect the other’s: what counts, what they may do with it, how long it lasts.
who: Two businesses or people who are about to share private information to explore a deal, a partnership or a project.
labels: the purpose, in a sentence or two

title: Offer letter template
line: Role, pay and start date, for a candidate to accept.
when: Use it when you have chosen someone and want their yes on paper.
It states what you are offering and asks for one signature to accept.
check: Fill in pay, hours and start date exactly.
Say whether the offer depends on a background check.
Set an expiry so the offer cannot be accepted months later.
summary: A full offer of employment: role, start date, pay, hours, benefits, conditions, notice and confidentiality, accepted by signing.
who: An employer making a job offer, and a candidate accepting it by signing.

title: Independent contractor agreement template
line: Who does the work, how it is paid, who owns the result.
when: Use it when someone who is not an employee will do work for you.
It names the work, the payment and the ownership of what is delivered.
check: Describe the work so both sides could tell if it was done.
State the rate and when it is paid.
Check whether your state treats this person as a contractor.
summary: An agreement between a company and an independent contractor: the work, pay, independence, ownership of what is made, confidentiality and ending.
who: A business that hires an independent contractor for a defined piece of work, and the contractor doing it.

title: Statement of work template
line: What will be done, by when, for how much.
when: Use it for one job under a larger agreement, so each job has its own scope.
It fixes the deliverables, the dates and the price before work starts.
check: List each deliverable as something that can be checked.
Give dates, not weeks.
Say what happens to work outside the scope.
summary: A detailed statement of work: objectives, scope, deliverables with dates, assumptions, acceptance, fees by milestone and change control.
who: An agency or freelancer and a client agreeing exactly what will be delivered, by when, for how much, under an existing or standalone agreement.
labels: Date of the master agreement, if any
State the objective in a few sentences
Say how the Client will know it worked
List what the Agency is assuming
How often the sides check in

title: Service agreement template
line: Scope, fees and term between a provider and a client.
when: Use it when you will do ongoing or repeated work for a client.
It covers the scope, the fees, the term and how either side ends it.
check: Match the scope to what you actually offer.
Write the fee and the payment date.
Decide how much notice ends the agreement.
summary: A full agreement for work one person or business does for another: scope, fees, term, ownership, confidentiality, liability and how it ends.
who: Anyone who does work for another business or person for a fee: consultants, studios, freelancers, small agencies.

title: Non-solicitation agreement
line: A promise not to hire away each other's people.
when: Use it when two businesses will work closely and share staff or clients.
It limits recruiting for a stated period.
check: Name who is covered: staff, clients or both.
Set a period you could defend as reasonable.
Check how your state treats these promises.
summary: An employee acknowledges and agrees not to solicit the company’s customers or colleagues for a set period after leaving.
who: An employer and an employee who want to record, in plain words, an agreement not to recruit each other’s people or take its customers.

title: Photo release form
line: Permission to use someone's picture.
when: Use it before you publish a picture of someone.
It says where and how the picture may be used.
check: List where the pictures will appear.
Say how long you may use them.
Use the media release form if the person is a minor.
summary: Permission to take and use photos or video of a person, with choices about where they appear and a way to withdraw.
who: A photographer, organization or business that takes photos or video of people and wants clear permission for where they are used.
labels: On the Organization’s social media accounts
In printed material such as flyers, brochures and reports
In news stories and press releases
My name may be used in captions

title: Permission slip template
line: A parent agrees to a trip or an activity.
when: Use it for a trip, an event or an activity that needs a parent's yes.
It names the activity, the date and who to call.
check: Give the date, place and times.
Add an emergency contact field.
Say what the school or group will and will not cover.
Keep health notes brief. Docustay is not for protected health information yet.
summary: A parent or guardian gives permission for a child to take part in a trip or activity, with health notes and emergency contacts.
who: A school, club or group that takes children on a trip or activity and needs a parent’s or guardian’s consent and emergency details.
labels: If I cannot be reached, I agree that the adults in charge may get urgent medical help for my child

title: Liability waiver template
line: Risk and responsibility, signed before an activity.
when: Use it before a class, a race, a rental or any activity with risk.
It states the risks and asks each person to accept them.
check: Describe the real risks of your activity.
Check what your state allows a waiver to cover.
Collect a guardian's signature for anyone under 18.
summary: A participant acknowledges the risks of an activity, agrees to follow the rules and confirms their emergency contact.
who: An organizer of a sports event, class, workshop or activity where participants accept the normal risks and agree to the rules.
labels: I have read this waiver and I understand it. I know that I am giving up some legal rights by signing it.

title: New hire paperwork
line: The forms to fill on day one, in one send.
when: Use it on or before the first day, so the paperwork is not the first day.
It gathers the usual forms into one send.
check: Remove what you do not use.
Add your own policies as extra pages.
Keep tax and identity forms in your own payroll system.
summary: One packet for a new starter, in several parts: welcome, handbook, confidentiality, equipment, payroll details and first-day information.
who: An employer welcoming a new starter: handbook, confidentiality, equipment, payroll details and first-day information in one packet to sign.
labels: I have received and read the staff handbook
I understand that I must treat colleagues, customers and suppliers with respect, and that harassment and discrimination
I will keep the company’s and its customers’ private information private, during and after my employment

title: Change order template
line: A signed change to the scope or the price.
when: Use it when the client asks for something the first agreement did not cover.
It records what changes and what it costs.
check: Name the agreement it changes.
State the new price and the new date.
Say that everything else stays the same.
summary: A written change to an existing agreement: what is changing, how the cost and time were worked out, and the new total and finish date.
who: A provider and client changing the scope, price or finish date of work that is already agreed.
labels: Explain how the extra cost or time was worked out

title: Media release form
line: A guardian lets you use a child's image and name.
when: Use it when the person in the picture or recording is under 18.
A parent or guardian signs on the child's behalf.
check: Say which media: photo, video or audio.
List where it will be shown.
Allow the guardian to withdraw permission later.
summary: A parent or guardian chooses where photos and video of their child may be used, with safeguards and a clear way to withdraw.
who: A school, club or charity that wants to photograph or film children and needs the parent’s or guardian’s informed, specific permission.
labels: Inside the Organization, such as displays, newsletters and noticeboards
On the Organization’s social media accounts
In news stories and press releases
Write “first name allowed” if it may
An earlier end date, if I want one

title: Rental application form
line: The applicant fills it in and signs.
when: Use it when someone wants to rent from you.
It collects the details you need to decide.
check: Ask only what the law lets you ask.
Say whether a fee is charged.
Tell applicants how long you take to decide.
summary: An applicant gives their details, address and income history, references and permission for the landlord to check what they have written.
who: A landlord or property manager collecting an applicant’s details, income, history and permission to run checks.

title: Lease addendum template
line: A change to a lease, signed in order.
when: Use it when a lease needs one added term, such as a pet or a new occupant.
It points at the lease and states the one change.
check: Name the lease and its date.
Write the added term plainly.
Say that the rest of the lease still applies.
summary: An addendum that changes an existing lease on one subject, with its terms, start date and what stays the same, signed by both sides.
who: A landlord and tenant adding or changing a term of an existing lease: pets, parking, rent date, guests, repairs or something else.
labels: Pet deposit or fee, in US dollars

title: Vendor agreement template
line: Terms for a supplier you will buy from again.
when: Use it when you will buy from a supplier more than once.
It sets deliveries, prices and payment dates.
check: List what is delivered and how it is checked.
State prices and payment terms.
Say how either side can end it.
summary: An agreement under which a vendor supplies goods or services to a company: orders, delivery, pricing, quality, payment, insurance and ending.
who: A business buying goods or services from a supplier on a continuing basis, and the supplier agreeing to deliver them.
labels: Amount of cover, in US dollars
a fixed amount, in US dollars

title: Payment plan agreement template
line: Payments by date, written into the agreement.
when: Use it when a client will pay in parts.
It lists each payment and its date.
check: Write each amount and its date.
Say what happens when a payment is late.
Connect your Stripe account to take a deposit as it is signed.
summary: A customer agrees to pay an outstanding balance in installments: the amount, the schedule, what happens if one is missed, and the first payment.
who: A business and a customer agreeing to settle a balance in installments, with the first payment taken securely before signing.
labels: Any agreed reduction, such as a discount for paying on time

title: Mutual release agreement
line: Both sides let go of claims against each other.
when: Use it to close out a dispute or a finished job.
Each side gives up the claims named in it.
check: Name the claims being released.
Say what, if anything, is paid.
Check what your state does not allow a release to cover.
summary: Two sides settle a matter and release each other from claims about it, with what is settled, any payment, and what is not released.
who: Two people or businesses settling a matter and agreeing not to bring claims against each other about it.
labels: Payment and when it is due, if any

title: Volunteer agreement template
line: Terms for an adult who helps without pay.
when: Use it when someone will help at your school, club or event.
It states what they will do and the rules they accept.
check: Describe the role and the hours.
List your safety and conduct rules.
Say that the role is unpaid.
summary: An agreement between an organization and a volunteer: the role, what each side commits to, confidentiality, safety, and how it ends.
who: A charity, school, club or event that relies on volunteers and wants role, expectations, confidentiality and safety written down.

title: Referral agreement template
line: A fee for sending you a client.
when: Use it when someone will send you clients for a fee.
It defines a referral and the payment.
check: Define what counts as a referral.
State the fee and when it is due.
Say how long the arrangement lasts.
summary: A company agrees to reward a referrer when a person they introduce becomes a customer: what counts, the reward, when it is paid and the rules.
who: A business that rewards another person or business for introducing customers.
labels: The reward, such as a percentage or a fixed amount

title: Deposit agreement
line: The deposit, its terms and when it comes back.
when: Use it when you take a deposit for a rental, a booking or a job.
It states the amount and the conditions for returning it.
check: Write the amount and what it secures.
Say when and how it is returned.
List what may be deducted.
summary: A customer pays a deposit to hold a booking, item or place: what it holds, when it is refunded, when it is kept, and the card payment.
who: A business or landlord taking a deposit to hold something for a customer, and saying when it is refunded or kept.
labels: Date after which the deposit is kept
Remaining balance and when it is due

title: Equipment loan agreement
line: What was lent, to whom, and when it comes back.
when: Use it when you lend equipment to a person or a team.
It lists each item and the date it returns.
check: List each item with its condition.
Set the return date.
Say who pays if it is lost or damaged.
summary: A lender lends an item to a borrower: description and condition, how it may be used, return date and who pays if it is lost or damaged.
who: A business, school or person lending equipment to another, with its condition recorded and what happens if it is lost or damaged.
labels: Accessories, such as cables and cases
Estimated replacement value, in US dollars
I agree that the condition is as described
the purpose, such as a project or event

title: Invoice approval form
line: A signed yes before an invoice is paid.
when: Use it when an invoice needs a named person's approval before payment.
It records who approved and when.
check: Name the invoice and its amount.
Name who must approve.
Say what happens if it is rejected.
summary: A record of an invoice, what it is for, and the approver’s decision, signed by the person who sent it and the person who approved it.
who: A business that needs a named person to approve an invoice before it is paid, with a record of who decided and when.
labels: The goods or services were received, and the invoice matches the order or contract
The price and quantities match the order or contract
The goods or services were delivered or carried out as described
The invoice has not been paid already and is not a duplicate
There is budget for it, and the right cost center or project is recorded
